risks.note: The Company derives a significant portion of its business from repeat customers, so any slowdown in client spending, delay in project execution, or loss of key customers may impact revenues and profitability. Mitigation is on-boarding new clients across geographies and engaging larger customers with better project visibility and higher ticket sizes.

A significant portion of business comes from international markets, particularly the United States; management separately flags dependence on export markets such as the USA, UK and Australia among its key threats. Any slowdown in construction activity in these markets flows straight through to revenue. Mitigation is regional diversification into Canada, New Zealand and Southeast Asia.
risks.risk: Geographic concentration in the United States and dependence on export markets

risks.note: The engineering and BIM industry is highly dependent on skilled manpower; inability to attract, train and retain qualified professionals may affect execution capability and service quality. Management also flags high dependence on skilled BIM professionals and rising employee costs as threats — a direct margin risk for a people-cost-led services model. Mitigation is continuous investment in manpower, training and R&D, plus multi-location delivery centres and structured training programmes.

Increasing dependence on digital engineering platforms and software tools exposes the business to cybersecurity threats, system disruptions and data security risks — material given the Company handles client design and project data across borders. Mitigation is strengthening IT infrastructure, project management systems and quality-control processes.

Management lists fast-changing software platforms among its key threats. The delivery model is built on specific engineering platforms (Tekla, SDS2, Revit), so platform shifts or new AI-driven toolchains require continuous reskilling and tooling investment to stay competitive.
risks.risk: Technology obsolescence from fast-changing software platforms

risks.note: The Company is exposed to foreign currency risk on revenue from overseas contracts and on expenses and payments denominated in foreign currencies. Exposure is managed through natural hedging and ongoing monitoring; management states it does not foresee any material adverse impact from foreign exchange fluctuations. Management separately lists foreign exchange volatility among its threats.

Management flags that it operates in a competitive and technology-led industry, with high BIM implementation costs for clients and the possibility of delayed digital adoption. Slower-than-expected BIM uptake would blunt the primary demand driver the Company's growth thesis rests on.
risks.risk: Competitive, technology-led industry with high client implementation cost and delayed digital adoption

risks.note: Growth depends materially on strategic acquisitions — four US entities acquired between December 2023 and March 2026, the latest taking the Company into a new service line (architecture). The Company itself states it must maintain operational integration and value creation, and its Board's Report emphasises alignment of a multi-geography, multi-entity structure; integration failure or overpayment would impair the strategy.
risks.risk: Execution and integration risk from an acquisition-led growth strategy

currentContext.expansion: Telge Projects is an asset-light engineering services business, so its expansion narrative is footprint, headcount and acquisitions rather than plant capex. During FY26 the Company completed strategic international acquisitions that expanded both its geographic footprint and its service portfolio, strengthening North American market access and taking it into the Architecture and Design services segment — the AOC-1 roster shows Edward Farr Architects, Inc. acquired on 3 March 2026 as a US step-down subsidiary under Telge Global Inc. (formerly Telge Projects Inc.), following Midwest Detailing LLC (January 2024) and Draftco Inc. (December 2024). Operationally the Company reports delivery centres at Pune, Latur and Nashik in India plus offices and subsidiaries across multiple US states, describing '7+ Delivery Centers' in the Corporate Overview; during FY26 it added new delivery centres and enhanced delivery infrastructure, increased overall delivery capacity to support growing client demand, and strengthened engineering capability through strategic hiring. The Company also listed on the BSE SME platform during the year, which the Chairman describes as a catalyst for future growth. The Chairman states that initiatives are underway to expand resources and substantially enhance operational capacity so as to undertake larger-scale projects and enter high-growth, high-demand markets. Investment continues in digital engineering, BIM technologies and process automation, and in an in-house R&D team. Forward capacity intent for FY27-FY30 centres on global expansion across North America and Europe, further value-accretive acquisitions, AI-enabled engineering, and building specialised capability for the data centre infrastructure sector. No rupee quantum, commissioning date, or capacity figure is attached to any of these initiatives anywhere in this bundle.
